title: Korean Dictionary of Occupations
role: Task descriptions used to construct occupational exposure.
coverage: Fifth integrated edition, published 28 May 2020; establishment task surveys conducted in 2012–2019.
acquisition_evidence: Timestamp recorded in the original KEIS download manifest.
sample_note: Actual occupation identifiers and short titles; no full dictionary text is reproduced.
notes: The publisher describes 6,075 principal occupations. The extraction used in the paper contains 6,074 entries. The paper and the linkage-corrected explorer are distinct mapping versions; their mapped-task counts must not be interchanged.

title: Conventional task-based AI exposure ratings
role: Training labels for transferring unweighted exposure to Korean tasks; shared labels for the Korea–US comparison.
provider: Eloundou et al.; GPTs-are-GPTs public repository
coverage: Task ratings associated with the GPT-4-era study, published in Science in 2024. Repository snapshot 0471612fef3c.
access: Local acquisition package dated 14 November 2026; an original per-file retrieval timestamp is not recorded.
acquisition_evidence: The download manifest identifies immutable repository URLs and SHA-256 checksums. A repository commit date is not a collection date.
sample_note: Actual task IDs and numerical labels from the training file.
notes: The score is the mean of human and GPT-4 exposure ratings after category recoding. It is a potential-exposure label, not an employment outcome. The retained training table has 923 O*NET occupation codes.

title: Anthropic human task-duration estimates
role: Training target for estimating the human time required to perform Korean tasks without AI.
coverage: Conversation windows named in the label-construction script are 13–20 November 2025 and 5–12 February 2026, plus data files labelled 26 June 2026. Claude.ai and first-party API data are used in constructing the label table. The Korean model is fitted to task-level human-duration estimates.
access: Original download dates are not recorded in the available duration-label package.
acquisition_evidence: The derived label table and construction script are preserved in the 15 November 2026 analysis package. This package date is not presented as the original retrieval date.
sources: Economic primitives report and data context
sample_note: Actual task-level aggregate estimates. Contributing releases counts the source releases represented in each task-level estimate.
notes: Durations are model-generated estimates of human work time, not stopwatch measurements or AI runtime. The table contains 5896 nonmissing duration targets. Source reporting and release windows differ; a file date does not by itself establish a conversation observation window.

title: METR task-completion horizons
role: Model-specific completion curves used to weight task exposure by predicted duration.
coverage: Benchmark snapshot covering model generations used in the paper, from GPT-4 (2023) to Claude Opus 4.6 (2026).
acquisition_evidence: Retrieval date, source URLs and checksums are recorded in the METR source-provenance manifest.
sample_note: Actual published horizon estimates, rounded to three decimals.
notes: The 50% horizon is the human task duration associated with 50% model success in the evaluated tasks. It is not agent runtime or a workplace automation rate. The original Korean panel uses GPT-4; the aligned prediction comparison uses GPT-5 (2025).

title: Korean Regional Employment Survey
role: Korean occupational employment panel, age/cohort comparisons, wages, and web demographic and education analyses.
provider: Statistics Korea / National Data Office, MDIS
coverage: April and October waves, 2013–2025; type B public-use national files with three-digit occupation codes. The matched Korea–US exercise uses April 2020–2025 and ages 16+. Main Korean employment analyses use ages 15+.
acquisition_evidence: The first-half README records the acquisition date; delivered archive filenames and the second-half acquisition records also identify this date.
sample_note: Survey-weighted annual aggregate examples from the web occupational panel, averaging April and October. These are not individual records or official all-occupation national totals.
notes: Raw row counts include people outside the analytical employed-person samples. Repeated cross-sections are person-wave observations, not unique people. Wages use positive-pay wage earners aged 25–64. Weights, education completion rules and age restrictions depend on the analysis. Raw MDIS microdata are not redistributed.

title: US Basic Monthly Current Population Survey
role: External employment comparison under conditions aligned with Korea.
provider: US Census Bureau and Bureau of Labor Statistics
coverage: 2020–2025. Monthly files were acquired; the reported harmonized comparison uses April waves and employed people aged 16+.
access: Acquisition run dated 18 November 2026; the download manifest does not store per-file retrieval times.
acquisition_evidence: URLs, byte sizes, acquisition status and checksums are recorded in the CPS download manifest. The run date identifies the acquisition package, not an exact timestamp.
sample_note: Derived occupation-level score examples linked to CPS codes; no respondent records are shown.
notes: Eligibility requires positive occupational employment in all six years, at least 100 baseline April records on average, and at least 80% SOC-link coverage. Cross-validation uses the upper conventional-exposure quintile, fixed 2020–2022 weights and identical controls in each score comparison.

title: Economically Active Population Survey
role: Website-only linked-unemployment comparisons and descriptive outcomes. Not the source of the paper’s occupational panel break estimate.
provider: Statistics Korea / National Data Office, MDIS
coverage: May youth-supplement public files, 2013–2025 for the displayed labor-market period. The acquisition also includes 2026, which is not used in the displayed 2013–2025 comparisons. The basic labor-force items cover all recorded ages, not just youth.
acquisition_evidence: Date recorded in the acquisition README and delivered archive filenames.
sample_note: Survey-weighted totals across the nine occupation groups for the two displayed comparison years.
notes: Linked unemployment uses unemployed people with a valid previous occupation, divided by current employed plus linked unemployed. First-time and unlinked jobseekers are excluded. It is not the official unemployment rate and must not be interpreted as an occupation-specific employment-to-population rate. Raw microdata are not redistributed.

title: Occupational classifications and crosswalks
role: Connect Korean dictionary entries to KSCO-8 occupations, and US task scores through SOC to Census occupation codes.
provider: KEIS, Statistics Korea classification materials, and US Census Bureau
coverage: Korean dictionary edition 2020, KSCO eighth-revision codes, and the 2018 Census occupation / SOC crosswalk used with 2020–2025 CPS.
access: Korean concordance preparation dated 14 November 2026; US crosswalk acquisition package dated 18 November 2026. Original per-file timestamps are not recorded for these links.
acquisition_evidence: Korean concordance README, crosswalk files, source inventory and US download manifest.
sample_note: Actual public code-link examples; these are classifications, not respondent records.
notes: One-to-many links are not individual worker transitions. The paper’s dictionary aggregation and the explorer’s linkage-corrected mapping are distinguished on the dictionary page. Changes in occupation systems and link coverage limit cross-country equivalence.

title: Derived task and occupation exposure data
role: THAIE scores used in the paper and interactive explorer. These are model predictions and transformations of the sources above, not a separate survey.
provider: Computed for this study using multilingual E5 and BGE-M3 encoders, ridge regression and METR curves.
coverage: Fixed dictionary task portfolios evaluated at GPT-4 (2023), Claude 3.7 Sonnet (2025), GPT-5 (2025) and Claude Opus 4.6 (2026) capability scenarios. These scenario years are not employment observation years.
access: No external acquisition date applies to generated scores. Core score package dated 15 November 2026; linkage-corrected release dated 16 November 2026.
acquisition_evidence: The scoring tables and source-construction scripts define the analytical versions.
sample_note: Actual derived occupation scores, unweighted over occupations for the summary statistics.
notes: The descriptive statistics are unweighted over task statements or occupations as named. They are not employment-weighted means. The paper uses E5 for its original high-exposure classification and BGE for content and duration in THAIE. The web demographic groups use fixed 2025 THAIE. No Korean respondent data or full manuscript is included in these pages.
